candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of floating solids or visible foam in other than trace amounts.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a qualitative enforceable limit keyed to 'trace amounts'; different readings of what constitutes trace versus non-trace could change whether a reported observation is treated as an exceedance (A) or how absent or ambiguous visual-monitoring evidence is classified when no numeric result exists (C).

candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on the water, or coatings on stream banks.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets separate narrative discharge prohibitions for oil, grease, and solids; interpretation of whether a reported condition qualifies as a prohibited visible film, globule, or coating could change compliance classification (A) and the semantics assigned to missing or non-numeric visual evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Samples taken in compliance with the monitoring requirements specified above shall be taken at the discharge after the treatment system and prior to the receiving stream.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the required sampling location relative to treatment and the receiving stream; whether monitoring was performed at the mandated point affects whether an obligation was satisfied (B) and whether available measurements are adequate evidence for compliance or missing-evidence analysis (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional special-study obligation tied to permit effective date and agency approval; whether FY2025 falls inside the six-month planning window or after plan approval could change whether Delta-BHC monitoring was required and how missing plan or sample evidence is interpreted (C).

candidates.exact_span: The plan must also include any use of delta-BHC at the facility, if any.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Adds a plan-content condition that may trigger or shape subsequent monitoring expectations based on facility use of delta-BHC; different interpretations of whether such use exists or was disclosed could change which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable (B) and whether absence of data reflects non-requirement or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Once approved, the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties Delta-BHC sampling frequency and location to permit year and plan-approval status; resolving which permit year FY2025 corresponds to, and whether 'more frequent' was required, changes whether quarterly intake monitoring was obligatory in FY2025 (B) and whether missing Delta-BHC results indicate a documentation gap versus a non-applicable period (C).

candidates.exact_span: The results of this study shall be attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links Delta-BHC study results to DMR submission; interpretation of this reporting duty affects whether Delta-BHC monitoring is treated as an enforceable reporting/monitoring obligation in FY2025 (B) and whether expected evidence should appear on DMRs when results are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharge Monitoring Report Form(s) shall be submitted quarterly. Each quarterly submittal shall include separate forms for each month of the reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines quarterly reporting with separate monthly forms; this granularity can change which months within FY2025 are treated as individually reportable monitoring periods (B) and whether a missing month is a partial-reporting gap versus a documented no-data or no-discharge state (C).

candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of the months March, June, September, and December.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Fixes the calendar boundaries of monitoring/reporting periods; assigning FY2025 measurements and obligations to the correct quarter depends on these end dates, which can change which limit or monitoring requirement applies to a given reported value (A) and which periods were due for monitoring or reporting in FY2025 (B).

candidates.exact_span: The first Discharge Monitoring Report(s) shall represent facility operations from the effective date of the permit through the last day of the current reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the initial reporting window from permit effective date through the end of the current quarter; if FY2025 overlaps the permit's opening period, different readings of effective date and 'current reporting period' change which months require coverage (B), which measurements map to which compliance periods (A), and whether early FY2025 gaps reflect transitional reporting rather than missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Thereafter, the permittee is required to submit regular quarterly reports as described above and shall submit those reports postmarked no later than the 28th day of the month following each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes ongoing quarterly submission timing with a postmark deadline; whether FY2025 quarters are subject to this schedule affects reporting-obligation applicability (B) and whether late or absent submissions are treated as missing required evidence versus unresolved timing (C).
